clause: Purchase and Sale. Seller agrees to sell and Buyer agrees to purchase the office furniture identified by the parties for an aggregate purchase price of One Thousand Two Hundred Dollars ($1,200). The parties acknowledge that the terms of the transaction were agreed verbally during a telephone conversation and that no written purchase agreement, purchase order, confirmation, or other memorandum evidencing the transaction was prepared or signed. The furniture has not yet been delivered and Buyer has not made any payment toward the purchase price.

Purchase Agreement. Seller shall sell and deliver to Buyer the industrial machinery described in Schedule A for a total purchase price of Five Thousand Dollars ($5,000). Buyer shall pay fifty percent of the purchase price upon execution of this Agreement and the remaining balance following delivery and inspection of the machinery. This Agreement constitutes the written understanding of the parties and has been executed and signed by authorized representatives of both Seller and Buyer.

Equipment Purchase. Seller agrees to provide Buyer with commercial printing equipment for a purchase price of Eight Thousand Five Hundred Dollars ($8,500). A written document describing the equipment, quantity, purchase price, and delivery terms was prepared and provided to both parties. Neither Seller nor Buyer signed or otherwise authenticated the document, and no goods have been delivered or accepted and no payment has been made.

Sale and Delivery of Equipment. Seller and Buyer verbally agreed that Seller would provide ten office workstations to Buyer for a total price of Six Thousand Dollars ($6,000). No written agreement was executed. Seller subsequently delivered all ten workstations to Buyer's principal office, Buyer received and accepted the workstations without objection, and the equipment has been installed and used in Buyer's daily operations. Buyer has not yet remitted the agreed purchase price.

Supply of Inventory. Seller and Buyer orally agreed to the purchase and sale of one hundred units of commercial inventory at a total contract price of Ten Thousand Dollars ($10,000). No written contract or signed memorandum was created. Seller delivered forty of the one hundred units, and Buyer inspected, accepted, and placed those forty units into its available inventory. The remaining sixty units have not been delivered, and Buyer disputes whether it is obligated to accept or pay for the undelivered balance.

Purchase of Computer Hardware. Buyer orally agreed to purchase computer hardware from Seller for a total price of Three Thousand Dollars ($3,000). Although no written purchase contract was signed, Buyer transferred the full purchase price to Seller and Seller accepted the payment. Seller has confirmed receipt of the funds and has identified the hardware to be provided under the transaction, but delivery has not yet occurred.

Long-Term Services Arrangement. Company and Consultant verbally agreed that Consultant would provide operational advisory services to Company for a fixed period of two years beginning on January 1, 2027 and ending on December 31, 2028. Company agreed to pay Consultant a monthly service fee throughout the full two-year term. The parties did not prepare, execute, or sign any written agreement or memorandum reflecting the terms of this arrangement.

Consulting Services Agreement. Consultant shall provide strategic and operational consulting services to Company for a term of twenty-four months commencing on the Effective Date. Company shall compensate Consultant in accordance with the monthly fee schedule attached as Exhibit A. The parties acknowledge that the obligations contemplated by this Agreement extend beyond one year. This Agreement has been reduced to writing and signed by authorized representatives of Company and Consultant.

Modification of Purchase Terms. Seller and Buyer previously entered into a signed written agreement for the sale of manufacturing equipment at a total price of Twenty Thousand Dollars ($20,000). Six months after execution, the parties verbally agreed to increase the quantity of equipment and raise the total purchase price to Thirty Thousand Dollars ($30,000). The modification was not documented in writing or signed by either party, although the original agreement requires amendments to be made in a signed writing.

Amendment to Equipment Purchase Agreement. Seller and Buyer agree to amend the existing Equipment Purchase Agreement to increase the quantity of equipment from ten units to fifteen units and to increase the aggregate purchase price from Twenty Thousand Dollars ($20,000) to Thirty Thousand Dollars ($30,000). Except as expressly modified by this Amendment, all provisions of the original Agreement remain in effect. This Amendment is in writing and has been signed by authorized representatives of both parties.

Payment Following Acceptance. Seller delivered fifty commercial storage units to Buyer in accordance with the written and signed purchase agreement between the parties. Buyer inspected the units upon delivery, accepted all fifty units without rejection, and placed them into commercial use. The purchase price became due fifteen days following acceptance. More than sixty days have passed since the payment deadline, and Buyer has failed to pay any portion of the amount due despite repeated written demands from Seller.

Delivery Obligations. Buyer and Seller executed a written purchase agreement requiring Seller to deliver twenty industrial generators to Buyer's warehouse no later than June 30. Buyer paid the required advance deposit and remained ready to accept delivery. Seller failed to deliver any of the generators by the contractual deadline and subsequently informed Buyer that it would not perform its delivery obligations under the Agreement. Buyer seeks to cancel the transaction and recover the amount previously paid.

Acceptance and Product Defects. Buyer received a shipment of commercial components from Seller pursuant to a written supply agreement. During inspection, Buyer discovered that several components did not conform to the specifications stated in the agreement. Despite knowledge of the nonconformity, Buyer accepted and used the entire shipment. Buyer did not notify Seller of the alleged breach for eighteen months after discovering the defects and now seeks remedies based on the nonconforming goods.

Merchant Purchase Confirmation. Buyer and Seller, each acting as merchants in the ordinary course of their respective businesses, verbally agreed to the sale of five hundred units of packaged inventory for a total price of Fifteen Thousand Dollars ($15,000). Within two business days after the agreement, Seller sent Buyer a written and signed confirmation stating the quantity, price, and delivery terms of the transaction. Buyer received the confirmation and did not object to its contents in writing within ten days after receipt.

General Supply Agreement. Seller agrees to supply Buyer with office equipment during the upcoming calendar year at the prices set forth in Seller's current commercial price list. The parties prepared and signed a written agreement identifying Seller and Buyer and describing the general category of goods to be supplied. The agreement does not identify any quantity of equipment to be purchased, does not state a minimum purchase requirement, and contains no method for determining the quantity of goods subject to the alleged sale.
